paragraphs: (A Tanna in Temple times.) In [Mishnah Peah 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Peah.2.6): an incident in which Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh sowed (two kinds of wheat), and came before Rabban Gamliel (the Elder); they went up to the Chamber of Hewn Stone and asked. Nachum the Scribe said: “I have received from Rabbi Meyasha,” etc.

In [Yoma 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.14b.3-5): “Rav Huna said: Who taught Tamid? Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh”; and it was taught on this, “Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh differs concerning the daily offering,” etc. Rabbi Yochanan said: “Who taught the Order of the Day? Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh.” In the [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.2.2.4): “Rabbi Yochanan said: Tamid is Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh’s.” Hyman infers from the phrase “Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh differs concerning the daily offering” some slight support for the possibility that he was a Kohen and served in the Temple.[^2]

notes.text: Saved Davidson Yoma14b fully writes Rav Huna. תמיד concerns the daily offering and the tractate/procedure discussion; Hyman’s slight support for priesthood remains expressly tentative, not a proven priestly identity.

[Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3419&lang=en) also links Shimon to the Peah incident. In the linked Bavli, Rav Huna initially attributes Tamid to Shimon and Rabbi Yochanan attributes the Yoma procedure to him. In the linked Yerushalmi, Rabbi Yochanan connects him with Tamid, followed by Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha’s qualification. Hyman considers service in the Temple only a possibility.
